Subject: Renewal conversation — request to add reserved GPUs + throughput assurance

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're getting final buy-in internally to move our inference traffic from shared hosted into a reserved pool as part of our Q2 renewal. A few asks we'd like you to confirm before we sign:

- Add 4x A100-equivalent reserved GPUs (baseline) with ability to burst +2 GPUs for 15% of monthly minutes.
- A tokens-per-second throughput guarantee for our primary model (gen-med-v3): target seen traffic is ~180k tokens/sec; we'd like a 200k tokens/sec reserved-pool guarantee measured at the pool level.
- A simple SLO metric and reporting cadence (how you measure, window sizes, and remediation credits).

I've attached a short doc with our expected traffic profile and a preliminary procurement checklist. Can you share Redwood's proposed SLO language and any sample addendum you use for reserved pools? Also flag any lead times for the additional GPUs.

Appreciate it — Samantha

Subject: Draft: Reserved Pool Throughput Addendum (proposal)

Samantha — attaching a draft addendum below (PDF attached). I tried to keep the wording operational and measurable. Key elements:

1) Scope and Reserved Capacity
- Reserved Pool: Avabio-reserved-pool-1 (4 GPUs, region: us-west-2).
- Burst: Auto-burst up to 2 additional GPUs for sustained short spikes (max 15% of billed minutes in a calendar month).

2) Throughput Guarantee (Tokens/sec)
- Guarantee: Redwood guarantees a minimum pooled throughput of 200,000 tokens per second (T/s) for Avabio-reserved-pool-1 for requests routed to gen-med-v3.
- Measurement: Throughput is measured at 60-second aggregation windows across the pool. A window is considered satisfied if the pool successfully serves >= 200,000 T/s (summed over all active servers) for >= 99.5% of 60-second windows sampled in a billing month.

3) Availability and Remediation
- Availability SLO: Reserved pool control-plane and serving endpoints will meet a 99.5% per-month availability measured at 1-minute windowing for control and 1-minute sampling for serving endpoints.
- Credits: If monthly satisfaction falls below 99.5% then Redwood will issue service credits pro-rated on the deficit (simple formula: shortfall percentage * monthly reserved fee).

4) Fallback Behavior
- If a single minute window drops below the throughput threshold, traffic will automatically fail-over to Redwood burst capacity or a compatible model variant; fail-over will be signaled to Avabio via the Console in the incidents page and via priority email if >5 continuous minutes impacted. Fail-over latency impact will be documented in the runbook.

5) Measurement & Dispute Process
- Redwood provides detailed per-minute telemetry for the pool (tokens/sec, p99 latency, KV cache hit-rate) accessible from the Console and a daily digest during incidents.
- Disputes: Avabio may raise a measurement dispute within 15 calendar days of invoice receipt; Redwood will provide raw telemetry within 5 business days to allow cross-checks.

Attachment: AVB_SLA_DRAFT_20270218.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

Subject: Re: Draft: Reserved Pool Throughput Addendum (proposal) — comments and redlines

Vanessa / Monica — thanks for the quick draft. Legal attached a redline and a few technical clarifications:

- Measurement window: we request 30-second granularity rather than 60s to better reflect spikes.
- Credit calculation: prefer an SLA credit cap not to exceed 50% of the monthly reserved fee; also ask that credits be automatically applied rather than requiring a claim.
- Burst economics: need clearer billing for burst minutes vs. reserved minutes (separate line item and a daily cap).

I've attached our redline (redline_avabio_comments.docx) and a small test dataset showing a typical 45s spike pattern. Could we get a response to the measurement window change and the auto-credit ask?

Thanks — David

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 28 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Reserved Pool Throughput Addendum (proposal) — agreement on process and next steps

Team — appreciate the thorough redline, David. Quick replies to the main points and proposed next steps: 

- Measurement window: We can support 30-second aggregation windows for tokens/sec reporting; however SLO satisfaction will still be calculated across 60-second windows for stability of sampling. Practically this means we publish 30s telemetry for transparency and feed a rolling 60s window into the SLO engine. We'll call this out explicitly in the addendum.
- Auto-credit: Redwood is willing to auto-apply credits for clear, system-level SLO misses (no dispute required) up to a monthly cap of 50% of the reserved fee. For edge cases, the dispute process still applies. We'll add a clause to automate credits for qualifying incidents.
- Burst billing: We'll add a burst line item in the invoice with clear per-minute rate and a configurable daily cap; Marcus will include modeled billing examples in the commercial proposal.

Action items and timeline:
1) Monica to update the addendum language to: (a) publish 30s telemetry, (b) document 60s SLO aggregation, (c) auto-credit clause (cap 50%), (d) explicit burst billing line item and daily cap. Target: draft revision 2 by 3/3.
2) Marcus to issue updated commercial (term, prorated GPU charges, burst pricing examples) by 3/3.
3) Avabio to review and return any final legal comments by 3/10 so we can align countersign by 3/17.

If that timeline works I'll schedule a quick 30-min runbook walkthrough with Monica and your infra team next week.

Thanks — Vanessa
